questions.q:
Which of the following are not in accordance with the property mentioned against them?
I. $\mathrm{F}_2 \gt \mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{Br}_2 \gt \mathrm{I}_2$ : Oxidising power
II. $\mathrm{MI} \gt \mathrm{MBr} \gt \mathrm{MCl} \gt \mathrm{MF}$ : Ionic character of metal halide
III. $\mathrm{F}_2 \gt \mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{Br}_2 \gt \mathrm{I}_2$ : Bond dissociation enthalpy
IV. $\mathrm{HI} \lt  \mathrm{HBr} \lt  \mathrm{HCl} \lt  \mathrm{HF}$ : Hydrogen-halogen bond strength
questions.solution:
Ionic character of metal halide :-
$\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{F} \gt \mathrm{M}-\mathrm{Cl} \gt \mathrm{M}-\mathrm{Br} \gt \mathrm{M}-\mathrm{I}$
This is due to low polarizability of fluorine due to very small size which gives more ionic character.
Thus, II is incorrect.
Order of bond dissociation enthalpy :-
$\mathrm{Cl}_2 \gt \mathrm{Br}_2 \gt \mathrm{F}_2 \gt \mathrm{I}_2$
This is due to very small size and $\mathrm{F}-\mathrm{F}$ bond length that causes repulsion between the atoms and possible multiple bonds between $\mathrm{Cl}_2, \mathrm{Br}_2$ and $\mathrm{I}_2$ due to availability of $\mathrm{d}$ orbitals.
Thus, III is incorrect.

& \Rightarrow \log \left(\mathrm{V}_2\right)=\frac{921.2-460.6}{460.6}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_2=10 \mathrm{~L}(\mathrm{X})

questions.q: The sum of the global minimum and global maximum values of the function $f(x)=\frac{4}{3} x^3-4 x$ in $[0,2]$ is
questions.solution:
Given $f(x)=\frac{4}{3} x^3-4 x, x \in[0,2]$
Now, $\mathrm{f}^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})=0 \Rightarrow 4 \mathrm{x}^2-4=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}= \pm 1$
Now $\mathrm{f}(0)=0, \mathrm{f}(1)=\frac{4}{3}-4=-\frac{8}{3}=$ global min
$f(-1)=\frac{-4}{3}+4=\frac{8}{3}f(2)=\frac{4}{3} \times 8-8=\frac{8}{3}$ global max.
So sum of global max + global $\min=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{8}{3}=0$

questions.q: In the cyclic process given in the $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{V}$ diagram, the work done is
questions.solution:
From diagram,
$\begin{aligned}
& \text { major axis, } 2 \mathrm{~b}=\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1}{2} \\
& \text { minor axis, } 2 \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_1}{2} \\
& \text { Work done }=\text { Area of cyclic work }=\pi \mathrm{ab} \\
& =\pi \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_1}{2}\right) \times\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1}{2}\right) \\
& =\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\mathrm{P}_2-\mathrm{P}_1\right)\left(\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1\right)
\end{aligned}$
